pages.caption: In the reign of the famous King Arthur there lived in Cornwall a lad named Jack, who was a boy of a bold temper, and took delight in hearing or reading of conjurers, giants, and fairies.
pages.description: [Young Jack stands in a medieval village]
pages.scene: Young Jack stands in a medieval village

pages.caption: In those days there lived on St. Michael's Mount, off Cornwall, a huge giant, eighteen feet high and nine feet round.
pages.description: [Giant looms over St. Michael's Mount]
pages.scene: Giant looms over St. Michael's Mount

pages.caption: He dwelt in a gloomy cavern on the top of the mountain, and used to wade over to the mainland in search of prey.
pages.description: [Giant carries oxen and sheep from mainland]
pages.scene: Giant carries oxen and sheep from mainland

pages.caption: When he would throw half a dozen oxen upon his back, and tie three times as many sheep and hogs round his waist.
pages.description: [Giant loads cattle on his back]
pages.scene: Giant loads cattle on his back

pages.caption: The giant had done this for many years when Jack resolved to destroy him.
pages.description: [Jack resolves to fight the giant]
pages.scene: Jack resolves to fight the giant

pages.caption: Jack took a horn, a shovel, a pickaxe, his armor, and a dark lantern, and one winter's evening he went to the mount.
pages.description: [Jack gathers tools and marches to the mount]
pages.scene: Jack gathers tools and marches to the mount

pages.caption: There he dug a pit twenty-two feet deep and twenty broad.
pages.description: [Jack digs a deep pit in the ground]
pages.scene: Jack digs a deep pit in the ground

pages.caption: He covered the top over so as to make it look like solid ground.
pages.description: [Jack covers pit with branches and soil]
pages.scene: Jack covers pit with branches and soil

pages.caption: He then blew his horn so loudly that the giant awoke and came out of his den crying out.
pages.description: [Jack blows his horn to wake the giant]
pages.scene: Jack blows his horn to wake the giant

pages.caption: "You saucy villain! you shall pay for this! I'll broil you for my breakfast!"
pages.description: [Giant emerges from cavern in fury]
pages.scene: Giant emerges from cavern in fury

pages.caption: He had just finished, when, taking one step further, he tumbled headlong into the pit.
pages.description: [Giant tumbles headlong into the pit]
pages.scene: Giant tumbles headlong into the pit

pages.caption: And Jack struck him a blow on the head with his pickaxe which killed him.
pages.description: [Jack strikes the giant with his pickaxe]
pages.scene: Jack strikes the giant with his pickaxe

pages.caption: Jack then returned home to cheer his friends with the news.
pages.description: [Jack returns home victorious]
pages.scene: Jack returns home victorious

pages.caption: Another giant, called Blunderbore, vowed to be revenged on Jack if ever he should have him in his power.
pages.description: [Giant Blunderbore appears in a lonely wood]
pages.scene: Giant Blunderbore appears in a lonely wood

pages.caption: Jack was passing through a wood, and being weary, sat down and went to sleep.
pages.description: [Jack falls asleep in the forest]
pages.scene: Jack falls asleep in the forest

pages.caption: The giant, passing by and seeing Jack, carried him to his castle.
pages.description: [Giant carries sleeping Jack to his castle]
pages.scene: Giant carries sleeping Jack to his castle

pages.caption: Where he locked him up in a large room, the floor of which was covered with the bodies, skulls and bones of men and women.
pages.description: [Room filled with skulls and bones]
pages.scene: Room filled with skulls and bones

pages.caption: Soon after the giant went to fetch his brother who was likewise a giant, to take a meal off his flesh.
pages.description: [Jack sees two giants approaching]
pages.scene: Jack sees two giants approaching

pages.caption: Jack, perceiving in one corner of the room a strong cord, took courage, and making a slip-knot at each end, he threw them over their heads.
pages.description: [Jack ties rope nooses over giants' heads]
pages.scene: Jack ties rope nooses over giants' heads

pages.caption: He tied it to the window-bars; he then pulled till he had choked them.
pages.description: [Jack pulls rope and hangs the giants]
pages.scene: Jack pulls rope and hangs the giants

pages.caption: When they were black in the face he slid down the rope and stabbed them to the heart.
pages.description: [Jack stabs the giants with his sword]
pages.scene: Jack stabs the giants with his sword

pages.caption: Jack next took a great bunch of keys from the pocket of Blunderbore, and in one of them found three ladies tied up by the hair of their heads.
pages.description: [Jack finds three starving ladies]
pages.scene: Jack finds three starving ladies

pages.caption: They told him that their husbands had been killed by the giants, who had then condemned them to be starved to death.
pages.description: [Jack frees the ladies from their bonds]
pages.scene: Jack frees the ladies from their bonds

pages.caption: "Ladies," said Jack, "I have put an end to the monster and his wicked brother; and I give you this castle and all the riches it contains."
pages.description: [Jack gives castle and keys to the ladies]
pages.scene: Jack gives castle and keys to the ladies

pages.caption: He then very politely gave them the keys of the castle, and went further on his journey to Wales.
pages.description: [Jack travels onward to Wales]
pages.scene: Jack travels onward to Wales

pages.caption: As Jack had but little money, he went on as fast as possible. At length he came to a handsome house.
pages.description: [Jack arrives at a handsome Welsh house]
pages.scene: Jack arrives at a handsome Welsh house

pages.caption: Jack knocked at the door, when there came forth a Welsh giant. Jack said he was a traveler who had lost his way.
pages.description: [Welsh giant welcomes Jack to his home]
pages.scene: Welsh giant welcomes Jack to his home

pages.caption: Jack took off his clothes quickly, but though he was weary he could not go to sleep.
pages.description: [Jack lies in bed listening to the giant]
pages.scene: Jack lies in bed listening to the giant

pages.caption: "Though here you lodge with me this night, You shall not see the morning light; My club shall dash your brains out quite."
pages.description: [Giant chants a threatening rhyme]
pages.scene: Giant chants a threatening rhyme

pages.caption: "Say you so?" thought Jack. Then, getting out of bed, he groped about the room, and found a large thick billet of wood.
pages.description: [Jack places a log in his bed]
pages.scene: Jack places a log in his bed

pages.caption: The giant, about midnight, entered the apartment, and with his bludgeon struck many blows on the bed.
pages.description: [Giant strikes the log with his bludgeon]
pages.scene: Giant strikes the log with his bludgeon

pages.caption: Early in the morning Jack put a bold face upon the matter, and walked into the giant's room to thank him for his lodging.
pages.description: [Jack emerges unharmed in the morning]
pages.scene: Jack emerges unharmed in the morning

pages.caption: The giant started when he saw him, and began to stammer out: "Oh! dear me; is it you?"
pages.description: [Giant stammers in confusion]
pages.scene: Giant stammers in confusion

pages.caption: "Nothing to speak of," said Jack, carelessly; "a rat, I believe, gave me three or four slaps with its tail."
pages.description: [Jack downplays the night's events]
pages.scene: Jack downplays the night's events

pages.caption: The giant wondered more and more at this; yet he did not answer a word, but went to bring two great bowls of hasty-pudding for their breakfast.
pages.description: [Giant brings bowls of hasty-pudding]
pages.scene: Giant brings bowls of hasty-pudding

pages.caption: Jack wanted to make the giant believe that he could eat as much as himself, so he contrived to button a leathern bag inside his coat.
pages.description: [Jack hides pudding in a leathern bag]
pages.scene: Jack hides pudding in a leathern bag

pages.caption: "Now I will show you a fine trick. I can cure all wounds with a touch; I could cut off my head in one minute, and the next put it sound again on my shoulders."
pages.description: [Jack reveals his trick to the giant]
pages.scene: Jack reveals his trick to the giant

pages.caption: He then took hold of the knife, ripped up the leathern bag, and all the hasty-pudding tumbled out upon the floor.
pages.description: [Jack rips open the bag, pudding spills out]
pages.scene: Jack rips open the bag, pudding spills out

pages.caption: "Ods splutter hur nails!" cried the Welsh giant, who was ashamed to be outdone by such a little fellow as Jack, so he snatched up the knife, plunged it into his own stomach, and in a moment dropped down dead.
pages.description: [Welsh giant stabs himself in despair]
pages.scene: Welsh giant stabs himself in despair

pages.caption: Jack, having hitherto been successful in all his undertakings, resolved not to be idle in future; he therefore furnished himself with a horse, a cap of knowledge, a sword of sharpness, shoes of swiftness, and an invisible coat.
pages.description: [Jack equips himself with magical items]
pages.scene: Jack equips himself with magical items

pages.caption: He traveled over high hills, and on the third day he came to a large and spacious forest through which his road lay.
pages.description: [Jack enters a great forest]
pages.scene: Jack enters a great forest

pages.caption: Scarcely had he entered the forest when he beheld a monstrous giant dragging along by the hair of their heads a handsome knight and his lady.
pages.description: [Giant drags a knight and lady by their hair]
pages.scene: Giant drags a knight and lady by their hair

pages.caption: Jack alighted from his horse, and tying him to an oak tree, put on his invisible coat, under which he carried his sword of sharpness.
pages.description: [Jack puts on his invisible coat]
pages.scene: Jack puts on his invisible coat

pages.caption: When he came up to the giant he made several strokes at him, but could not reach his body, but wounded his thighs in several places.
pages.description: [Jack fights the giant invisibly]
pages.scene: Jack fights the giant invisibly

pages.caption: At length, putting both hands to his sword and aiming with all his might, he cut off both his legs.
pages.description: [Jack cuts off the giant's legs]
pages.scene: Jack cuts off the giant's legs

pages.caption: Then Jack, setting his foot upon his neck, plunged his sword into the giant's body, when the monster gave a groan and expired.
pages.description: [Jack stabs the giant through the heart]
pages.scene: Jack stabs the giant through the heart

pages.caption: The knight and his lady thanked Jack for their deliverance, and invited him to their house, to receive a proper reward for his services.
pages.description: [Knight and lady thank Jack]
pages.scene: Knight and lady thank Jack

pages.caption: "No," said Jack, "I cannot be easy till I find out this monster's habitation."
pages.description: [Jack seeks the giant's habitation]
pages.scene: Jack seeks the giant's habitation

pages.caption: So, taking the knight's directions, he mounted his horse and soon after came in sight of another giant, who was sitting on a block of timber.
pages.description: [Second giant sits on a block of timber]
pages.scene: Second giant sits on a block of timber

pages.caption: Jack approached and aimed a blow at the giant's head, but, missing his aim, he only cut off his nose.
pages.description: [Jack misses and cuts off the giant's nose]
pages.scene: Jack misses and cuts off the giant's nose

pages.caption: On this the giant seized his club and laid about him most unmercifully.
pages.description: [Giant swings his club wildly]
pages.scene: Giant swings his club wildly

pages.caption: "Nay," said Jack, "if this be the case I'd better dispatch you!" so, jumping upon the block, he stabbed him in the back.
pages.description: [Jack jumps on block and stabs the giant]
pages.scene: Jack jumps on block and stabs the giant

pages.caption: Jack then proceeded on his journey, and traveled over hills and dales, till arriving at the foot of a high mountain he knocked at the door of a lonely house.
pages.description: [Jack arrives at a lonely hermitage]
pages.scene: Jack arrives at a lonely hermitage

pages.caption: When Jack was seated the hermit thus addressed him: "My son, on the top of this mountain is an enchanted castle, kept by the giant Galligantus and a vile magician."
pages.description: [Hermit warns Jack of the enchanted castle]
pages.scene: Hermit warns Jack of the enchanted castle

pages.caption: "I lament the fate of a duke's daughter, whom they seized as she was walking in her father's garden, and brought hither transformed into a deer."
pages.description: [Hermit tells of a duke's daughter transformed]
pages.scene: Hermit tells of a duke's daughter transformed

pages.caption: Jack promised that in the morning, at the risk of his life, he would break the enchantment.
pages.description: [Jack promises to break the enchantment]
pages.scene: Jack promises to break the enchantment

pages.caption: And after a sound sleep he rose early, put on his invisible coat, and got ready for the attempt.
pages.description: [Jack climbs toward the enchanted castle]
pages.scene: Jack climbs toward the enchanted castle

pages.caption: When he had climbed to the top of the mountain he saw two fiery griffins, but he passed between them without the least fear of danger.
pages.description: [Jack passes between two fiery griffins]
pages.scene: Jack passes between two fiery griffins

pages.caption: On the castle gate he found a golden trumpet, under which were written these lines.
pages.description: [Jack finds golden trumpet at the castle gate]
pages.scene: Jack finds golden trumpet at the castle gate

pages.caption: "Whoever can this trumpet blow Shall cause the giant's overthrow."
pages.description: [Inscription on the trumpet]
pages.scene: Inscription on the trumpet

pages.caption: As soon as Jack had read this he seized the trumpet and blew a shrill blast, which made the gates fly open and the very castle itself tremble.
pages.description: [Jack blows the trumpet with a shrill blast]
pages.scene: Jack blows the trumpet with a shrill blast

pages.caption: The giant and the conjurer now knew that their wicked course was at an end, and they stood biting their thumbs and shaking with fear.
pages.description: [Giant and magician tremble with fear]
pages.scene: Giant and magician tremble with fear

pages.caption: Jack, with his sword of sharpness, soon killed the giant.
pages.description: [Jack slays the giant with his sword]
pages.scene: Jack slays the giant with his sword

pages.caption: And the magician was then carried away by a whirlwind.
pages.description: [Magician carried away by a whirlwind]
pages.scene: Magician carried away by a whirlwind

pages.caption: And every knight and beautiful lady who had been changed into birds and beasts returned to their proper shapes.
pages.description: [Enchanted prisoners return to human form]
pages.scene: Enchanted prisoners return to human form

pages.caption: The castle vanished away like smoke.
pages.description: [Enchanted castle vanishes like smoke]
pages.scene: Enchanted castle vanishes like smoke

pages.caption: And the head of the giant Galligantus was then sent to King Arthur.
pages.description: [Jack sends giant's head to King Arthur]
pages.scene: Jack sends giant's head to King Arthur

pages.caption: The knights and ladies rested that night at the old man's hermitage, and next day they set out for the Court.
pages.description: [Knights and ladies travel to the King's Court]
pages.scene: Knights and ladies travel to the King's Court

pages.caption: Jack then went up to the King, and gave his Majesty an account of all his fierce battles.
pages.description: [Jack recounts his adventures to the King]
pages.scene: Jack recounts his adventures to the King

pages.caption: Jack's fame had now spread through the whole country, and at the King's desire the duke gave him his daughter in marriage.
pages.description: [Jack receives the duke's daughter's hand in marriage]
pages.scene: Jack receives the duke's daughter's hand in marriage

pages.caption: After this the King gave him a large estate, on which he and his lady lived the rest of their days in joy and contentment.
pages.description: [Jack and his lady live happily ever after]
pages.scene: Jack and his lady live happily ever after
